### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via nextScreen (symbol, a field of interface ScreenProgressSpec), stepCount (symbol, a field of interface ScreenProgressSpec), nextScreen (literal, a string literal in readScreenProgress))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **147** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 74db43ef3d64f8315af68952ec45d9c46942fbc7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b2c0114d9305f27045f4785e168e95a469b3ffd2` — the merge of head `094a249d92dcba0fb134ea601be98e95259eddcb` into base `74db43ef3d64f8315af68952ec45d9c46942fbc7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin b2c0114d9305f27045f4785e168e95a469b3ffd2 && git checkout b2c0114d9305f27045f4785e168e95a469b3ffd2

git fetch origin 74db43ef3d64f8315af68952ec45d9c46942fbc7 094a249d92dcba0fb134ea601be98e95259eddcb && git checkout -B drift-repro 74db43ef3d64f8315af68952ec45d9c46942fbc7 && git merge --no-ff 094a249d92dcba0fb134ea601be98e95259eddcb

```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a

> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 74db43ef3d64f8315af68952ec45d9c46942fbc7` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `653293e7b8177159c052c1f26227d001312b1375`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/screen-nodes.ts (`readScreenProgress`, the `progress` closure, the executor's own pause rule), packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/subflow-node.ts and map-node.ts (`$parentRunId`, which node forwards a child `screen`), packages/services/service-automation/src/dag-traversal.ts (`traverseNext` edge selection, which `visitShape` models), packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/logic-nodes.ts (the `decision` executor's `branchLabel`), packages/services/service-automation/src/screen-input-contract.ts (`judgeHeadlessScreen`, `callerSupplied`), packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (`getFlow`, `getActionDescriptor`), packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts (`FlowEdgeSchema` `type` / `isDefault` / `condition`), packages/spec/src/automation/builtin-node-config.zod.ts (`ScreenConfigSchema`), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/FlowRunner.tsx and ScreenView.tsx (the first consumer's read of `ScreenSpec.progress`), packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json and export-origins/contracts.json (the public-surface delta). The rest of the diff (changeset, `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`, the strictness-ledger count, the three test files) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Inputs read: card #26657 (body, triage 6441476979, claim 6442765961, os-dev-report 6444639574), PR #26752 (body, 12-file list, net diff against merge-base `43731031`), the head's check-runs (two polls). Rulings the card cites, read as cited: #26369 ruling 6431004737 (letter B, the `Skills-docs:` trigger) and #26368 ruling 6431014712 (letter A, the p1 yardstick).

Check-runs on the head at the time of this record: no run red. Completed `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, every `Lint ·` lane, `Test Core (8/8)`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`. Still `in_progress`: `Build Core`, `Test Core (1–7/8)`, `Test UI (1–16/16)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check UI`, `Lint UI`. The required set is therefore not yet green: this record judges the contract and the design; the landing still waits for every check, as it always does.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`ScreenSpec.progress?: ScreenProgressSpec`** (contracts/automation-service.ts) — one optional member on a published interface. Accept-set change: a producer may now serve one more key; every existing producer and consumer stays valid. RIGHT, and correctly optional: the TSDoc's two reasons for absence (an older server; a child-run screen whose own graph ends) are both real in the cited executor.
2. **`export interface ScreenProgressSpec`** — a new public export of `@objectstack/spec/contracts`; `api-surface/contracts.json` and `export-origins/contracts.json` each gain exactly that one row, nothing removed or narrowed. RIGHT: a widening, and the regenerated artifacts match the source.
3. **`screenProgressSpecShape` on `TriggerFlowResponseSchema.data.screen.progress`** (api/automation-api.zod.ts) — module-local, `z.object` (strip), `nextScreen: z.enum(['none','possible','certain'])`, `step` / `stepCount` `int().min(1).optional()`. RIGHT on three counts: (a) the closed enum and the 1-based bounds refuse what the contract's TSDoc forbids and nothing the engine serves (`step = prior + 1 ≥ 1`, `stepCount = step + remaining ≥ step`); (b) `z.object` rather than `strictObject` is the sibling convention of `screenSpecShape` / `screenFieldSpecShape`, whose own note explains the wire shape stays lenient for screens rehydrated from an older suspension; (c) the existing compile-time identity pin `TriggerFlowDataMatchesContract` binds this spelling to the interface, and `Type Check · source gates` is `success` on this head, so the two cannot drift.
4. **Zod strip semantics across versions** — an older client parsing a newer server's response strips `progress` and behaves as before; a newer client against an older server sees no `progress` and the runner keeps Submit. RIGHT: the rollout is order-independent, as the PR body claims.
5. **No authorable key changes.** `FlowSchema`, `ScreenConfigSchema`, `FlowEdgeSchema` are untouched; `check:authorable-surface` has nothing to regenerate and the dev's `check:generated` found none stale. RIGHT.
6. **Strictness ledger `api/` 446 → 447** — one new non-strict `z.object` site in an untriaged directory, regenerated whole by its generator. RIGHT as an artifact; the choice it counts is item 3(b).
7. **Persisted suspension** — `suspended-run-store.ts` stores `screen_json` as JSON with no schema on the way back, so a run suspended on this head rehydrates `progress` intact and a run suspended before it rehydrates without one. RIGHT; no migration is owed.
8. **One wire spelling only** — no second schema in `packages/spec/src/api` or `packages/rest` spells the paused screen (grep for `idVariable` co-occurring with `nodeId` outside tests finds only the two `hits` files and their executor), so no route strips the key that another serves. RIGHT.
9. **The first consumer** — `ui/.../ScreenView.tsx` derives its `ScreenSpec` from the spec interface (`Omit<SpecScreenSpec,'fields'> & …`), so `FlowRunner` reads `screen.progress` typed; `common.next` / `common.submit` / `form.stepOf` already exist in every bundle (the zh pin in the new test reads them). RIGHT: no translation key is added, as declared.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/26657-screen-progress-next-submit.md`: `@objectstack/spec` patch, `@objectstack/service-automation` patch, `@object-ui/app-shell` patch; body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, byte-identical to the PR body. PR-body gates `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` are `success` on the head.

Clause-②: `yes (widening)` is RIGHT — a new optional member on a published interface, a new public interface export, and a new optional key on a published response schema; nothing narrowed, nothing removed.

Metadata-protocol: `none` is RIGHT, and the level `patch` follows from it. The brief asks this explicitly, so the reasoning in full: AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 defines the kind as *the change to what a metadata author can write — a new key, accepted value or metadata type is `added`*, and `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` records the maintainer ruling it implements (ruling A, 2026-10-21, #25105): *the level of a changeset follows the METADATA PROTOCOL alone: `minor` when the protocol an author writes against is added to, narrowed or changed in meaning, `patch` otherwise*. `ScreenSpec.progress` is a member the ENGINE serves on a paused run; no flow, screen node or edge an author writes gains a key, a value or a meaning (`FlowSchema`, `ScreenConfigSchema`, `FlowEdgeSchema` untouched; `check:authorable-surface` unchanged). It is a published-surface widening — the Clause-② line carries that — not a protocol addition in the kind's own vocabulary. The triage line *every protocol addition is p1 (#26368 A)* is the PRIORITY yardstick (「协议新增定 p1」) and grades the card; it does not redefine the `Metadata-protocol:` kind, which is read by `clause2-line.mjs` and governs the level. So the declaration must stay `Metadata-protocol: none`, and the level must stay `patch` on all three packages. A `minor` here would be the wrong declaration, not a safer one: it would claim an author-facing change this diff does not make.

### ③ Boundary flags

PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` on the base repo (`objectstack-ai/objectstack`): no off-relay author to name. `open_questions: []` — nothing to answer or escalate. Each declared deviation, answered:

1. *Files beyond the claimed surface* (api/automation-api.zod.ts and its test, flows.mdx, three regenerated artifacts) — ACCEPTED: the wire spelling is bound to the interface by the identity pin and reds without it; the docs half is what #26369 B's `updated here` sense names for the docs; the artifacts are the ones ① items 2 and 6 verify.
2. *No new translation keys* — ACCEPTED, verified in ① item 9.
3. *Skills half not written here; `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md`* — ACCEPTED as a deferral, with one correction of its basis. Under SKILL.md:313 and ruling 6431004737 (letter B) the `Skills-docs:` line is OWED only when the kind is `added` / `semantic` / `narrowed` or the Clause-② arm is `(narrowing)`; this PR is `none` + `(widening)`, so by rule no line is owed at all, and the triage sentence *Skills, docs and eval are owed (#26369 B)* was written on the premise of a protocol kind that the diff did not turn out to have. The dev wrote the line anyway, and a line that is present must be true (review-checklist.md:18): `follow-up owed — FILES` is a legal value, and the seat rewrites it to `#N` before ACCEPT, or the dev rewrites it to `none — REASON`. Deferring the `skills/**` edit is the correct split, not an omission: `skills/**` is Tier H (Prime Directive #14), one such path would make the whole PR Tier H, and the directive's own prescription is to split off the governed files. The follow-up has real content — `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md:91` teaches the screen NODE's config and nothing about the paused payload a custom runner reads — so filing it is right; it is a seat duty on ACCEPT, not a must-fix on this head.
4. *Two `wip:` commit subjects* — not reviewed here (squash-merge takes the PR title).
5. *app-shell type-check needed a local build first* — environment; CI's `Type Check UI` measures it and is in progress.

One thing the body says that the tree does not quite bear out, for the lane seat's TIER_DEFAULT read of the prose face (outside `hits`, so not a finding of this record): `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` opens its new section with *Every paused screen carries `progress`*, and three paragraphs later correctly says a child-run screen carries it only when its own flow shows another screen; the contract's TSDoc (a `hits` file, and right) says absent on an older server too. The first sentence should read *a paused screen carries `progress` whenever the engine can answer* or similar.

### ④ Design judgment

**packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts — `ScreenSpec.progress` / `ScreenProgressSpec`.** Judged against the executor that fills it and the runner that reads it, and against the scenario the card accepts it for (a wizard reads Next, Next, Submit and counts steps only when the count is exact; the client never walks the graph).

- *Tri-state over a boolean.* Tried to break it with a branch after a screen: a boolean must guess; `'possible'` says what the graph knows and the runner reads it as Next, which is the one label that is never a lie before a later screen (a run that instead finishes is answered by the completion toast). HOLDS.
- *Counts present only when exact; the object absent only when the engine cannot answer.* Tried the three "absent" states against the executor: no `progress` is served when the executor runs outside a run (`context.flowName` unset), when the node is not a `screen` of the registered flow, and when a child-run screen's own graph ends. The TSDoc names only the last of these plus the older-server case. The runner's behaviour is identical in all four (keeps its old label), so nothing a consumer does differs; the TSDoc's *cannot answer at all* is simply under-enumerated. SHOULD-FIX (doc precision): list the first two or say *including* before the examples.
- *`step` without `stepCount`.* The contract allows it (`{ nextScreen: 'possible', step: 1 }`), the schema allows it, the runner draws nothing without both, the docs say so. Consistent on all four surfaces. HOLDS.
- *A pause that serves no screen (approval, wait) counts as a possible end of the stretch.* Read against the engine: only a `screen` executor sets `NodeExecutionResult.screen` and only `subflow-node.ts` forwards a child's `screen` (map-node.ts returns `suspend` with a `correlation` and NO `screen`, so a `map`'s child screen never rides the parent's paused result). The role map — `subflow` → `'subflow'`, any other `supportsPause: true` descriptor → `'pause'` — is therefore exactly the set of nodes that can serve a screen versus merely pause, and the engine itself refuses a pause from any type that does not declare `supportsPause`, so an `approval` executor registered by a plugin is classed `'pause'` by invariant. HOLDS.
- *The child-run clamp.* `$parentRunId` is set by both subflow-node.ts and map-node.ts on the child context and is persisted with the child run, so a child screen keeps only a non-`'none'` `nextScreen` and no counts. Correct in both directions: `'certain'` / `'possible'` inside the child are still true in the parent's run; `'none'` and every count are not knowable from the child graph. The PR body is honest that a subflow-composed wizard therefore keeps Submit on the child's last screen — the claim is as narrow as the enforcement (Prime Directive #10). HOLDS; a parent-aware read is a separate card if anyone asks for it.

**packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts — `screenProgressSpecShape`.** Judged against the interface it mirrors and the response it rides on.

- The enum, the integer bounds and the optionality match the TSDoc exactly; the new test refuses `'maybe'`, a missing `nextScreen`, `step: 0` and `1.5`, and keeps both the full and the counts-less shape. The identity pin compiles. The `.describe()` texts restate the contract without adding a rule the interface lacks. HOLDS.
- Lenient (`z.object`) over strict: the sibling shapes on the same response are lenient for a stated reason, and a strict mirror would make this one key the only place where an older producer's extra byte refuses a whole paused run. Right choice. HOLDS.

**Cited engine code, read to judge the contract (not reviewed): `readScreenProgress` against `traverseNext`.** Tried to break `visitShape`'s model of how a visit continues against `dag-traversal.ts`:

- Unconditional out-edges run as a parallel fan-out; a `decision`'s conditional edges are exclusive-first unless `mode: 'inclusive'`; `isDefault` runs only when no conditional sibling held; a fault edge runs only on failure. `visitShape` encodes each of these: `fansOut` on more than one unconditional-or-default edge, on inclusive-or-non-decision conditional pairs, and on an unconditional edge beside a conditional one on an exclusive decision; `mayStop` when nothing unconditional or default follows, or when the node may pause or hand off to a child. MATCHES.
- One shape the model over-reports: a `decision` authored with `config.conditions[]` and LABELLED unconditional edges (`logic-nodes.ts:86` returns `branchLabel: cond.label`; `traverseNext` then narrows to the claimed edges) is read as a parallel fan-out of every labelled edge. `nextScreen` stays right (the 0-1 BFS takes the minimum over all branches, which is the right answer for an exclusive choice as well), but `fansOut` becomes true and every count is dropped — a label-routed wizard never gets a counter, even on a straight path before the decision. Conservative, never wrong, and the docs' authoring advice (branch only after the last screen) already steers authors past it. SHOULD-FIX (precision): treat the labelled out-edges of a `decision` that carries `conditions` as exclusive in `visitShape`; a candidate line for the follow-up card, not a blocker.
- `'none'` by reachability includes fault and back edges; `'certain'` is the fewest surely-pausing screens on any path to a point where the run may stop, with the current screen's own `mayStop` seeding 0; loops collapse by SCC and a loop that holds a screen yields no count; a screen whose fields the caller may have supplied is `'maybe-screen'` and judged with the SAME `judgeHeadlessScreen` and the SAME persisted context the executor will use when it reaches that screen, so the two verdicts cannot disagree. Each of the thirteen engine pins and five graph pins reads as a true statement of this model. HOLDS.
- The role read uses the raw `n.config` of the registered flow while the executor reads the parsed `ScreenConfigSchema`; the three keys compared (`objectName`, `waitForInput`, `fields`) carry no schema default, so raw and parsed agree. HOLDS.

**Must-fix:** none. **Should-fix:** the TSDoc's under-enumerated absence cases (contracts/automation-service.ts), and the label-routed-decision precision in `readScreenProgress` (cited code; a follow-up line). Neither changes what a consumer must do with the key.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-6imvw2`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · `domain:spec` seat 1 (#6017) · session `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh` · 2026-10-27T15:14Z

Head `094a249d92dcba0fb134ea601be98e95259eddcb`. Card #26657, claim `6442765961`, dev report `6444639574`.

- **Contract review:** owed at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER for `api/automation-api.zod.ts` and `contracts/automation-service.ts`. PASS `6444906744` at `653293e7`, with no must-fixes. The one commit since then, `094a249d`, lands the findings only:
  - The `ScreenSpec.progress` TSDoc now lists each case where progress is absent (no flow name, a node that is not a screen of the registered flow, no start node).
  - `flows.mdx` no longer opens with "Every paused screen carries progress", which contradicted the contract.
  
  The diff from `653293e7` to `094a249d` is those 2 files, +12/−5, with no code change.
- **Lane seat (rest of the diff, TIER_DEFAULT):** the engine's `readScreenProgress` reads the graph the run resumes from. It answers `possible` on a branch, a fault edge, a loop back, a non-screen pause or a subflow, and it gives counts only when every path agrees. FlowRunner reuses `common.next` / `common.submit` / `form.stepOf`, so no new i18n keys are needed.
- **Should-fixes, not carried:**
  - A decision authored with `config.conditions[]` and labelled edges is read as a fan-out. Its counts drop while `nextScreen` stays right. This is a precision follow-up, not a defect.
  - The object-form step's "Save & Continue" on its last step is outside this card.
- **Skills-docs:** `#26756`. The skills row is a Tier H follow-up, judged the correct split by the review. Nothing is owed by rule (kind `none`, widening).
- **Shape:** `Fixes #26657`, 12 files. `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/service-automation` and `@objectstack/app-shell` are `patch`. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`: `progress` is engine-served, and no authored schema moved. `check-governed-merges --pr 26752`: NOT governed, 809 changed lines.
- **Gates:** check-runs on this head are 58 success, 7 skipped and 0 red. One `PR-body guards` run was cancelled and superseded by a success after the body edit.
